findings.title: Unhandled rejection on sidebar getSharedWith fetch
findings.problem: The sidebar's useEffect calls assistantsStore.getSharedWith(assistant.id).then(...) with no .catch(). The store method now intentionally propagates errors uncaught (per this change's own Access-list-error AC), so any fetch failure here surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection rather than a handled error state.
findings.impact: An owner viewing assistant details when the shared-with fetch fails (network error, 403, backend outage) gets a console-logged unhandled rejection and a silently empty SHARED WITH section, with no retry affordance — unlike the popup's parallel call to the same store method, which does catch and surface a Retry UI.
findings.recommendation: Add a .catch() to the getSharedWith call in this effect, consistent with the cancelled-ref pattern already present, mirroring ShareAssistantPopup.tsx's loadSharedWith error handling.

findings.title: Popup's getSharedWith fetch missing isOwner defensive gate
findings.problem: loadSharedWith calls assistantsStore.getSharedWith(assistant.id) unconditionally whenever the popup is visible with an assistant set. The design explicitly specifies this fetch should also be gated on isOwner(assistant) as a defensive second gate; isOwner is never imported into this file.
findings.impact: Currently unreachable in the shipped UI — the popup's sole call site (AssistantActions.tsx) already gates the Share action itself on isOwner(assistant, userId) && isUserManagementEnabled() — but the explicit design requirement is unimplemented, untested, and would allow an owner-only fetch to run for a non-owner if the popup is ever opened through any future call site that skips that outer gate.
findings.recommendation: Import isOwner from @/utils/entity and gate the fetch (or the visible && assistant effect) on isOwner(assistant, userStore.user?.userId), matching the pattern already used in AssistantDetailsSidebarSections.tsx:95.
